title: Hanji Incipit — MMCA Catalog Opening
description: A restrained exhibition opener built on coarse hanji paper texture, Myeongjo serif titling in sumi black, and a single vermillion seal — evoking the authoritative first folio of a Korean national museum catalog.
philosophy: This design values material silence over decorative noise: the hanji ground does the visual work while type recedes into scholarly restraint. It rejects Western sans-serif modernism, animation, and chromatic complexity in favour of the severe economy found in MMCA and Leeum print culture. The vermillion seal is the sole chromatic event — a stamp of cultural provenance, not ornamentation. It is made for speakers who understand that institutional authority requires no embellishment.
goodFor: Gallery and museum exhibition opening slides
Art catalog or monograph launch presentations
Cultural institution curatorial or donor briefings
avoidFor: High-energy product launches or startup pitch decks
Slides requiring dense multi-column data tables
Audiences expecting Western editorial or sans-serif visual language
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the opening leaf of a national museum catalog — still, weighty, and unapologetically material. The hanji ground carries all visual temperature; type sits within it like sumi absorbed into paper, not printed on top. Compositional rhythm is sparse and left-anchored, with wide breathing margins that signal institutional authority over decoration. The vermillion seal is the sole chromatic event — a provenance stamp, never ornament — avoid gloss, gradients, or any kinetic Western editorial sensibility.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed hanji texture ground with no overlaid panels or card containers; a generous 10% outer margin preserves the feel of a folio page. A 12-column grid anchors the title block in columns 2–8, left-weighted and placed at the upper golden-section of the vertical axis, with the catalog subtitle sitting beneath a single hairline horizontal rule. The vermillion seal occupies the lower-right quadrant, partially cropped at the page edge so it reads as a genuine ink stamp rather than a placed graphic. A folio number or catalog code appears at bottom-left in the smallest text tier, completing the scholarly document register.

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes an interior folio from a national museum print catalog — unhurried, materially grounded, where silence is the primary compositional act. A single curatorial statement or attributed pull quote occupies a left-weighted column; the surrounding hanji ground is not empty space but active texture carrying the weight of institutional restraint. The vermillion seal appears once at the foot as a stamp of cultural provenance, anchoring the page without competing with text. Avoid infographic cadence, icon clusters, bullet-list rhythm, and any decorative layering — authority here is earned through scholarly economy, not visual elaboration.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with the primary text block anchored in columns 2–9, leaving a deliberate wide right margin that lets the hanji ground breathe as a compositional element. Section heading sits flush to column 2 with a single fine horizontal rule beneath it — hierarchy is carried by the rule line, not weight contrast alone. A curatorial statement, pull quote, or short attribution block occupies the mid-field; no more than two text strata appear. Folio number and a small vermillion seal are pinned to the bottom-right corner, outside the active text grid; no header band breaks the top edge.
